001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.jul;
002
003import java.time.Instant;
004import java.util.MissingResourceException;
005import java.util.ResourceBundle;
006import java.util.logging.LogRecord;
007
008import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
009
010import io.jstach.rainbowgum.KeyValues;
011import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEvent;
012import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogMessageFormatter.StandardMessageFormatter;
013import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogRouter;
014
015/**
016 * Translates {@code java.util.logging.LogRecord} into Rainbow Gum
017 * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEvent} and routes it through {@link LogRouter#global()}.
018 * Shared by two independent JUL integration strategies: this module's own
019 * {@link java.util.logging.Handler}-based bridge ({@code SystemLoggerQueueJULHandler},
020 * installed on the default JUL root logger), and the separate
021 * <code>rainbowgum-jul-logmanager</code> module's {@code java.util.logging.LogManager}
022 * replacement (which routes every {@code java.util.logging.Logger} call directly,
023 * bypassing JUL's normal Handler/Level dispatch entirely). Kept here, exported, so
024 * neither integration duplicates the level mapping or event construction.
025 */
026public final class JULBridge {
027
028        private JULBridge() {
029        }
030
031        private static final int TRACE_LEVEL_THRESHOLD = java.util.logging.Level.FINEST.intValue();
032
033        private static final int DEBUG_LEVEL_THRESHOLD = java.util.logging.Level.FINE.intValue();
034
035        private static final int INFO_LEVEL_THRESHOLD = java.util.logging.Level.INFO.intValue();
036
037        private static final int WARN_LEVEL_THRESHOLD = java.util.logging.Level.WARNING.intValue();
038
039        /**
040         * Maps a {@code java.util.logging.Level} to the closest
041         * {@link java.lang.System.Logger.Level}, the same threshold buckets JUL's own builtin
042         * levels (FINEST/FINE/INFO/WARNING/SEVERE) fall into, so custom intermediate levels
043         * still translate sensibly.
044         * @param level JUL level, including custom levels with arbitrary
045         * {@link java.util.logging.Level#intValue()}.
046         * @return closest matching System.Logger level.
047         */
048        public static System.Logger.Level toLevel(java.util.logging.Level level) {
049                int lv = level.intValue();
050                if (Integer.MIN_VALUE == lv) {
051                        return System.Logger.Level.TRACE;
052                }
053                else if (TRACE_LEVEL_THRESHOLD >= lv) {
054                        return System.Logger.Level.TRACE;
055                }
056                else if (DEBUG_LEVEL_THRESHOLD >= lv) {
057                        return System.Logger.Level.DEBUG;
058                }
059                else if (INFO_LEVEL_THRESHOLD >= lv) {
060                        return System.Logger.Level.INFO;
061                }
062                else if (WARN_LEVEL_THRESHOLD >= lv) {
063                        return System.Logger.Level.WARNING;
064                }
065                else if (Integer.MAX_VALUE == lv) {
066                        return System.Logger.Level.OFF;
067                }
068                return System.Logger.Level.ERROR;
069        }
070
071        /**
072         * Whether a logger name at a given JUL level is currently enabled, per Rainbow Gum's
073         * own level resolution rather than anything cached on a JUL
074         * {@code Logger}/{@code Handler}.
075         * @param loggerName logger name, as JUL would pass to
076         * {@link java.util.logging.Logger#getName()}.
077         * @param level JUL level being checked.
078         * @return true if a record at this name/level would actually be routed.
079         */
080        public static boolean isLoggable(String loggerName, java.util.logging.Level level) {
081                return LogRouter.global().route(loggerName, toLevel(level)).isEnabled();
082        }
083
084        /**
085         * Translates a JUL {@link LogRecord} into a Rainbow Gum event and routes it, if the
086         * record's logger name/level is currently enabled. A {@code null} record or a record
087         * with a {@code null} logger name is silently ignored, matching
088         * {@link java.util.logging.Handler#publish(LogRecord)}'s own contract for
089         * {@code null}.
090         * @param rec JUL log record, possibly {@code null}.
091         */
092        public static void publish(@Nullable LogRecord rec) {
093                if (rec == null) {
094                        return;
095                }
096                String loggerName = rec.getLoggerName();
097                if (loggerName == null) {
098                        return;
099                }
100                var level = toLevel(rec.getLevel());
101                var router = LogRouter.global();
102                var route = router.route(loggerName, level);
103                if (!route.isEnabled()) {
104                        return;
105                }
106                @Nullable Throwable cause = rec.getThrown();
107                @Nullable String msg = getMessage(rec);
108                var args = rec.getParameters();
109
110                Instant timestamp = rec.getInstant();
111                long threadId = rec.getLongThreadID();
112                String threadName = "";
113                long currentThreadId = Thread.currentThread().threadId();
114                if (currentThreadId == threadId) {
115                        threadName = Thread.currentThread().getName();
116                }
117                // TODO fix key values aka MDC
118                // TODO fix caller info
119                var event = LogEvent.ofAll(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, msg, KeyValues.of(), cause,
120                                StandardMessageFormatter.JUL, args);
121                route.log(event);
122        }
123
124        private static @Nullable String getMessage(LogRecord record) {
125                String message = record.getMessage();
126                if (message == null) {
127                        return null;
128                }
129                ResourceBundle bundle = record.getResourceBundle();
130                if (bundle != null) {
131                        try {
132                                return bundle.getString(message);
133                        }
134                        catch (MissingResourceException e) {
135                                // no translation found - fall through and use the raw message instead
136                        }
137                }
138                return message;
139        }
140
141}
